scrape – Extract

src/flask_website/scrape.py

Scrape applicant results from The GradCafe survey pages.

This module is the extract stage of the ETL pipeline. It:

  • checks robots.txt before fetching anything and refuses to scrape if the survey path is disallowed;

  • walks the survey listing one page at a time by following each page’s Next link (GradCafe paginates with an opaque cursor token);

  • parses each result row into a dictionary of raw text fields; and

  • writes the de-duplicated entries to a JSON file for clean.

Scraping stops cleanly on HTTP 403/429/503, CAPTCHA/block pages, network errors, or when the page limit (MAX_PAGES) is reached.

Example:

python scrape.py --max-pages 50 --delay 3 --output applicant_data.json
scrape.BASE_URL = 'https://www.thegradcafe.com'

Root URL of The GradCafe.

scrape.SURVEY_PATH = '/survey'

Path of the first survey listing page.

scrape.ROBOTS_URL = 'https://www.thegradcafe.com/robots.txt'

Fully-qualified robots.txt URL.

scrape.USER_AGENT = 'JHU-SoftwareConcepts-Module2-Scraper/1.0 (+mailto:sbattl15@jh.edu; educational coursework)'

Identifying User-Agent sent with every request (includes a contact address).

scrape.MAX_PAGES = 2000

Hard upper limit on pages fetched per run (desired_entries // 20).

scrape.REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15

Socket timeout for each HTTP request, in seconds.

scrape.DEFAULT_DELAY_SECONDS = 3.0

Politeness delay after each page request, in seconds.

scrape.MAX_SIBLING_ROW_HOPS = 3

How many trailing <tr> rows to scan for metadata/comments per result.

Bases: RuntimeError

Raised when scraping must stop because of blocking/rate limiting.

scrape.check_robots_txt(user_agent='JHU-SoftwareConcepts-Module2-Scraper/1.0 (+mailto:sbattl15@jh.edu; educational coursework)')[source]

Download and parse GradCafe’s robots.txt.

The file is fetched manually with USER_AGENT (rather than RobotFileParser.read(), which uses urllib’s default agent and is often blocked). A 401/403 is treated as disallow all; any other 4xx as allow all, mirroring the standard library’s behaviour.

Parameters:

user_agent (str) – User-Agent to send when fetching robots.txt.

Returns:

A populated robots parser.

Return type:

urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser

Raises:

  • urllib.error.HTTPError – For 5xx responses.

  • urllib.error.URLError – If the host cannot be reached.

scrape._find_next_page_url(html, current_url)[source]

Find the URL of the next page of results.

GradCafe paginates with an opaque ?cursor=... token rather than a plain page number – the only way to know page N+1’s URL is to read it out of the Next link in page N’s HTML.

Parameters:

  • html (str) – Current page HTML.

  • current_url (str) – URL of the current page (for resolving relative links).

Returns:

Absolute URL of the next page, or None on the last page.

Return type:

str or None

scrape.scrape_data(max_pages=None, delay_seconds=3.0)[source]

Scrape survey pages, following GradCafe’s Next link page by page.

GradCafe paginates with an opaque cursor token, not a page number – page N+1’s URL is only known after page N has been fetched and parsed, so pages are fetched strictly one at a time, in order.

Stops once max_pages pages have been fetched, when a page has no Next link, or on any blocking/network error. MAX_PAGES is a hard limit. Entries are de-duplicated by GradCafe result ID.

Parameters:

  • max_pages (int | None) – Pages to fetch; None means MAX_PAGES. Values above MAX_PAGES are capped.

  • delay_seconds (float) – Delay after each request.

Returns:

Unique raw entries (see _parse_page() for keys).

Return type:

list[dict]

Raises:

  • ValueError – If max_pages < 1 or delay_seconds < 0.

  • PermissionError – If robots.txt disallows the survey page.

  • RuntimeError – If robots.txt cannot be retrieved.
